title: Moving to Columbia TN: A Buyer Guide for Nashville and Beyond
description: Moving to Columbia TN from Nashville or out of state? Local market data, monthly costs, schools, commute and the steps to take before you buy in Maury County.
body:
If you are moving to Columbia TN, you are probably weighing price, commute and what a monthly payment looks like once taxes and insurance are added. Columbia sits in Maury County, along the Duck River, south of the Williamson County line.

This guide covers the local numbers, the costs that vary by address, and the steps to take before you make an offer. I have kept it to facts that come from named sources, with dates.

## What the Columbia market looks like right now

{{img:0}}

According to Redfin (rolling 3 months, data as of 2026-10-31), Columbia's median sale price was $354,753, down 1.4% from a year earlier. Median days on market was 75, and the average sale-to-list ratio was 96.8%. There were 450 active listings.

Redfin also shows 5.0 months of supply. Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 months is balanced, and over 6 months favors buyers.

Other sources describe the market in their own ways. Zillow's Market Temperature Index for Columbia was 32, which Zillow's data places as leaning toward buyers. The trend is heating, with the index up 11 points over 3 months. Realtor.com Research puts Maury County at a hotness score of 35.4 out of 100.

These are citywide figures. Conditions can differ a lot by price range and by street, so use them as context, not a prediction. The [Columbia real estate guide](/columbia) is a good place to keep reading.

## If you are coming from Nashville

For comparison, Redfin reports that the Nashville metro area, for the 4 weeks ending 2026-11-08, had a median sale price of $467,332 and a median of 69 days on market. The sale-to-list ratio was 97.7%, months of supply was 5.9, and 2,232 homes sold.

Those numbers cover a different area and a different time window than the Columbia figures, so I would not line them up too tightly. What they do show is that conditions in each place should be read on their own terms. Local data, such as months of supply, days on market and sale-to-list ratio for your own city, tells you more than national headlines.

A quick geography check helps if you are comparing areas. Columbia is in Maury County. Murfreesboro is in Rutherford County. Neither is in Williamson County. Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties, so county services, schools and taxes can differ by address. If you are still deciding between towns, see [Columbia vs Franklin](/columbia/columbia-vs-franklin) and [Columbia vs Spring Hill](/columbia/columbia-vs-spring-hill).

## The monthly cost of owning in Columbia

{{img:1}}

The payment is more than principal and interest. Freddie Mac (via FRED) reported the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week of 2026-11-12. Nobody can reliably predict where rates go next, so run your own numbers in the [mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator) at a few different rates.

**Property tax.** For the 2025 tax year, inside Columbia city limits, the combined rate is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value (county $1.91, city $0.8251). Tennessee assesses residential property at 25% of appraised value. As an illustration only, a home appraised at $100,000 would be assessed at $25,000, which works out to about $684 a year at that rate.

Those are the 2025 rates, the latest I found in the Tennessee Comptroller data, via the Maury County community profile for Columbia. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, when rates are reset, so the 2026 rates may be lower. Confirm the current figure for any home with the Maury County Trustee, starting at [Maury County Government](https://www.maurycounty-tn.gov). Your bill depends on the exact address, and whether it is inside city limits.

**Other costs.** Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs. Private mortgage insurance is typically required on conventional loans when the down payment is under 20 percent. FHA loans allow a down payment as low as 3.5 percent. VA loans typically require no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance, though a funding fee may apply.

For context on the area, the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey (5-year estimates, 2020 to 2024) lists Columbia's median gross rent at $1,197 per month and median household income at $63,719. If you are renting now, one way to frame the decision is to compare the full monthly cost of buying (payment, taxes, insurance, maintenance) with the cost of renting a comparable home, and to weigh how long you expect to stay. More budget detail is on the [Columbia cost of living](/columbia/cost-of-living) page.

## Schools, commute and city services

Columbia addresses are zoned through Maury County Public Schools, the county district. The most reliable way to find the zoned school for a home is the district's own lookup tool, available through [Maury County Public Schools](https://www.mauryk12.org). Zoning can change, so check it for any home you are serious about. I do not rate schools, and you should not rely on anyone's opinion in place of the district's official information. The [Columbia school districts](/columbia/schools) page is a starting point.

On commuting, the Census Bureau's 5-year estimates (2020 to 2024) show a mean travel time to work of 28 minutes for Columbia. That is an average for the city, not a promise for your route or your hours. Test your actual drive at the time of day you would make it, and check current conditions on [TDOT SmartWay traffic](https://smartway.tn.gov). See also [Columbia commute times](/columbia/commute).

For trash, water and other city services, start with the [City of Columbia](https://www.columbiatn.gov), since what applies can depend on whether a home is inside city limits. If a property is near the Duck River, ask about its flood zone status and insurance requirements, and check with the county and your insurance agent.

## Steps to take before you move

**Get pre-approved, not just pre-qualified.** Pre-qualification is a quick estimate based on what you tell a lender. Pre-approval means the lender has reviewed your documents and credit. It is still not a final commitment. Final approval depends on the appraisal, underwriting and your finances staying the same until closing. Avoid opening new credit, financing furniture or changing jobs from the time you apply through closing.

**Compare Loan Estimates.** A lender must give you a Loan Estimate within three business days of your application. The CFPB encourages you to get them from more than one lender, because rates and fees can differ. You choose your own lender. The Tennessee Housing Development Agency (THDA) offers home loan programs through participating lenders, so ask any lender you consider whether they take part.

**Plan inspections.** Radon testing, a sewer scope and a termite inspection are common add-ons to a standard home inspection. Termite and wood-destroying organism inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee. Sellers complete the residential property condition disclosure (or an exemption), and the lead-based paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

**Watch closing day.** The lender must send the Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing. Compare it with your Loan Estimate and ask questions. Wire fraud is real, so verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust, and never rely on emailed instructions.

**Book movers early.** Request quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies, and book early for month-end dates. Cancel homeowner's insurance on a sold home only after closing is confirmed. The [free moving checklists](/checklists) can help you keep it all in order.

## Talk it through with Scott

If you are coming from Nashville or from out of state, a conversation can save you a lot of guesswork. Fill out the [Get Matched form](/buy#form), and I will schedule a call. You will be talking with me within the next 48 hours. If you would rather ask a question first, use the [contact page](/contact).

— Scott Davis, REALTOR®, RE/MAX Choice Properties
